nodes.title: Baseline mailbox contract fixtures and migration invariants
nodes.description:
Capture the current supported mailbox behavior before changing contracts. Add reusable fixtures for v1 direct, base-alias, session, project-broadcast, leader-only, read, completed, deleted, reply, corrupt-line, and mixed acknowledgement cases. Pin the task-graph edge convention as dependency → dependent.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Existing supported mailbox behavior is represented by deterministic fixtures without changing production behavior.
- Fixtures cover every current message type, recipient form, audience, priority, acknowledgement action, and query field.
- V1 JSONL fixtures include historical globally completed direct and fan-out messages.
- Rejected fixture operations assert zero storage side effects.
- The graph validator confirms every edge endpoint exists and the graph is acyclic.

**Verification:**
- Run the existing focused mailbox suite before contract changes.
- Validate this graph with the repository TaskGraph deserializer and a DAG check.

nodes.title: Define actor, principal, capability, and recipient-receipt contracts
nodes.description:
Add the typed domain contract for trusted mailbox actors, HTTP principals, capabilities, recipient-scoped state, v2 receipt records, actor projections, and legacy global-completion metadata. Do not change persistence behavior in this task.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Types distinguish trusted actor context from untrusted payload fields.
- Capabilities cover send, self-read, administrative read, self-ack, presence write, presence read, and management.
- Recipient state supports independent read, completion, timestamp, completer, and outcome per actor.
- V2 receipt records have an explicit discriminator/version and remain ignorable by previous readers.
- Legacy-global completion is explicitly represented and cannot be created by new typed APIs.
- Public exports use the coordination subpath without introducing root-import regressions.

**Verification:**
- Typecheck @wrongstack/core.
- Run focused type/codec tests.

nodes.title: Implement shared mailbox boundary codecs and stable errors
nodes.description:
Implement shared codecs for send, query, acknowledgement/check, registration, and mailbox actions. Codecs accept unknown data plus trusted actor context where required, perform structural and cross-field validation, and return normalized domain inputs or stable boundary errors. Do not cut over transports yet.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Every supported field and default has one canonical parser.
- Type/recipient validation cannot be bypassed through a codec entry point.
- Security-sensitive actor claims are rejected when they disagree with trusted context.
- Stable errors distinguish validation, unauthorized, forbidden, not found, conflict, and internal failures.
- Unknown-field policy is documented and tested.
- Codecs contain no HTTP, CLI, WebSocket, or HQ response-writing logic.

**Verification:**
- Run codec table tests.
- Typecheck @wrongstack/core.

nodes.title: Enforce canonical query semantics including exact replyTo filtering
nodes.description:
Move mailbox query normalization/predicates behind one canonical implementation and apply exact `replyTo` filtering. Preserve composition with all current filters, defensive copies, ordering, limit behavior, actor visibility, and index fallbacks.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Querying `replyTo=A` returns only direct replies whose parent is exactly A.
- Empty `replyTo` is rejected by untrusted codecs and has documented typed-call compatibility behavior.
- replyTo composes with to, from, unread actor, incomplete, type, priority, since, sender session, deletion, audience, and limit.
- Query candidate indexes never change results relative to a full scan.
- Direct core, tool, and HTTP query fixtures produce equivalent normalized behavior.

**Verification:**
- Run GlobalMailbox query and codec tests.
- Typecheck @wrongstack/core.

nodes.title: Materialize mixed v1 and v2 mailbox receipt records
nodes.description:
Extend JSONL parsing/materialization to fold v1 message/read/ack/delete records and v2 actor receipt records into one normalized projection. Preserve malformed-line tolerance and make legacy global fan-out completion explicit so upgrades do not re-deliver historical finished work.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- V1 readBy and acknowledgement records map to actor receipt state.
- V2 read/completion/outcome/delete records survive close and reopen.
- Historical direct completion maps to its known actor when possible.
- Historical globally completed fan-out mail is marked legacy-global and remains suppressed.
- Mixed-log record order is deterministic and duplicate/no-op receipts are idempotent.
- Malformed v2 receipt records are skipped and counted without dropping valid messages.

**Verification:**
- Run codec, migration, compaction, and reopen tests.
- Typecheck @wrongstack/core.

nodes.title: Persist actor-scoped acknowledgements and expose actor/aggregate projections
nodes.description:
Change read, completion, outcome, soft-delete/restore, unread, incomplete, and compaction paths to use trusted actor receipt state for v2 messages. Keep explicit aggregate and legacy projections for administrative views and rollback.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Completing a broadcast as actor A leaves actor B incomplete.
- Direct actor completion persists across reload and excludes the message only for that actor.
- Actor-facing projections expose readByMe, completedByMe, and actionRequiredForMe.
- Administrative projections expose aggregate counts without impersonating an actor.
- Ack actor overrides are rejected before append.
- Auto-compaction cannot remove a v2 fan-out message because only one actor completed it.
- New writes do not create legacy-global completion.

**Verification:**
- Run actor-isolation, compaction, reload, and cross-process acknowledgement tests.
- Typecheck @wrongstack/core.

nodes.title: Implement authenticated mailbox principal and capability policy
nodes.description:
Implement project-bound principals, capability checks, identity credential resolution, legacy-operator mapping, and structured authorization diagnostics. Reuse existing secret facilities for credential material; do not log tokens.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Principals carry project, identity, actor kind, trusted role, capability set, and auth mode.
- Capability checks are deterministic and deny by default.
- Credentials cannot resolve to a different project than the mounted mailbox.
- Reserved runtime identities require trusted runtime issuance.
- Legacy bearer mode maps to a named legacy-operator principal and is observable.
- Diagnostics contain principal/auth metadata but no token material.

**Verification:**
- Run principal/capability policy tests.
- Typecheck @wrongstack/core.

nodes.title: Enforce identity-scoped principals in the mailbox HTTP router
nodes.description:
Upgrade router authorization to return a principal, derive actor fields server-side, apply shared codecs/capabilities to every route, and contain legacy bearer mode to explicit loopback compatibility. Preserve consistent JSON error envelopes, rate limiting, body caps, health probes, and SSE teardown.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- New authorization success always includes a principal.
- Body-supplied from, readerId, agentId, role, or client identity cannot override the principal.
- Self credentials cannot read all mail, ack another actor, register another identity, or manage retention.
- Operator operations require explicit capabilities.
- Legacy mode is named, counted, warning-emitting, and loopback-only by default.
- Non-loopback legacy startup fails closed without an approved unsafe override.
- Existing auth failure, rate-limit, validation, body-size, and SSE tests remain green.

**Verification:**
- Run router, mutation-matrix, and security tests.
- Typecheck core and CLI host packages.

nodes.title: Cut over internal mail tools and slash commands to shared contracts
nodes.description:
Move `mail_send`, `mail_inbox`, low-level `mailbox`, mailbox loop/checker, and `/mailbox` adapters to trusted actor contexts, shared codecs, exact reply filtering, and actor-scoped projections. Remove duplicated validation only after parity tests cover it.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Thin and low-level tools produce equivalent normalized send/query/ack inputs.
- Inbox/check/read state is computed for the resolved mailbox identity.
- Slash commands cannot bypass canonical type/recipient rules.
- `replyTo` is available wherever the surface exposes querying or replies.
- Session, alias, project broadcast, leader-only audience, Chimera send policy, and request-scoped injection remain intact.
- Duplicate validation removed by this task has an equivalent shared-codec fixture.

**Verification:**
- Run mail-tools, mailbox-tool, mailbox-loop, smoke, and slash mailbox tests.
- Typecheck core and CLI.

nodes.title: Cut over standalone and HQ HTTP mailbox gateways
nodes.description:
Wire the standalone bridge and HQ project gateway through principal-bearing authorization, shared codecs, actor-scoped query/mutation projections, and explicit legacy mode. Preserve project resolution and per-project router caching.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Both HTTP hosts mount the same canonical router contract.
- Project IDs resolve server-side and principals cannot override project scope.
- Standalone and HQ mutation matrices return equivalent errors and zero-side-effect guarantees.
- Existing browser/operator auth rules remain enforced in addition to mailbox capabilities.
- Router/mailbox/SSE resources still close on shutdown.
- Legacy clients remain available only through the explicit compatibility mode.

**Verification:**
- Run standalone bridge, HQ mailbox mutation/action, routing, SSE, and shutdown tests.
- Typecheck core and CLI.

nodes.title: Cut over WebSocket, WebUI, and HQ mailbox projections
nodes.description:
Update WebSocket handlers, mailbox stores, HQ mapper/protocol summaries, and required UI fields to distinguish actor-specific state from aggregate state. This is contract plumbing, not a mailbox UX redesign.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Actor-facing payloads expose actor-specific read/completion/action state.
- Administrative/HQ payloads expose aggregate receipt data with unambiguous names.
- Existing `completed` and read-count fields remain documented compatibility projections during rollout.
- WebUI unread counters do not equate any-reader or incomplete state with the selected actor's unread state.
- Task context, audience, recipient scope, replyTo, sender session, deletion, and outcome fields retain their current meaning.
- WebSocket/HQ payload validators reject actor claims that belong to authenticated server context.

**Verification:**
- Run WebSocket mailbox handlers, WebUI mailbox store/model tests, and HQ mailbox grouping/action tests.
- Typecheck WebUI server and affected UI packages.

nodes.title: Add the cross-surface mailbox contract matrix
nodes.description:
Run one golden fixture matrix through direct core, thin tools, low-level tool, HTTP router, standalone bridge, WebSocket handler, HQ gateway, and slash-command adapters. Compare normalized results/errors rather than transport-specific wrappers.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Matrix covers every field, default, alias, audience, type/recipient rule, actor override, query filter, and error class.
- Each fixture declares applicable surfaces and any explicit unsupported reason.
- Applicable surfaces normalize equivalently or return the same stable error code/field path.
- Rejected fixtures have zero storage side effects.
- Matrix specifically covers replyTo and two-recipient fan-out completion isolation.
- Removing any shared-codec call from one surface causes a deterministic test failure.

**Verification:**
- Run the dedicated cross-surface contract matrix and focused regressions.

nodes.title: Add migration, concurrency, rollback, and authorization fault tests
nodes.description:
Prove the high-risk behavioral guarantees independently of the surface parity suite: mixed-log migration, historical no-reflood, actor completion isolation, concurrent append/ack/compact, crash/reopen, previous-reader rollback compatibility, and principal capability denial.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- V1-only, v2-only, and mixed fixtures normalize identically before and after compaction/reopen.
- Historical globally completed fan-out messages do not reappear after upgrade.
- New fan-out completion is isolated per actor across processes.
- Child-process send/ack/compact races lose no messages or receipts.
- Previous-version compatibility fixture reads migration-window output.
- Every capability denial and actor override returns the expected error with zero side effects.
- Legacy non-loopback startup refusal is covered.

**Verification:**
- Run dedicated migration/concurrency/security suites plus existing mailbox security tests.

nodes.title: Document migration, expose telemetry, and wire rollback controls
nodes.description:
Publish operator/external-agent migration guidance, expose bounded compatibility diagnostics, add named rollout/rollback configuration, and define the removal gate for legacy global completion projection and legacy bearer mode.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Docs explain identity credentials, capability scopes, body actor changes, replyTo parity, actor-scoped completion, and legacy limits.
- Diagnostics expose v1 records, v2 receipts, legacy-global projections, legacy-auth use, forbidden actor overrides, and malformed receipts without secrets.
- Rollout and rollback flags have explicit defaults and test coverage.
- Legacy mode remains loopback-only by default.
- Removal requires one stable release with no known legacy clients and no migration/parity failures.
- Public docs and tool descriptions do not advertise capabilities unavailable on their surface.

**Verification:**
- Run config validation, system-prompt/tool-description, docs-link, and mailbox diagnostics tests.
- Review diff for secret/token exposure.

nodes.title: Writer-version fence for safe mixed-version mailbox mutation
nodes.description:
Implement a version marker/sentinel that prevents previous-version processes from mutating a mailbox file after v2 receipt records appear. This blocks v2 receipt writes from being erased by an old compactor or collapsed by an old reader.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- A version marker (sentinel line or sidecar) is written when the first v2 receipt record is appended.
- An old process encountering the marker refuses all mutation operations (send, ack, softDelete, restore, purge, compact, clearAll) with a structured error.
- Read-only operations by old processes continue to work (backward-compatible reads).
- The fence is idempotent: re-checking an existing marker does not create duplicates.
- Fence detection handles missing, corrupt, and sidecar-only markers gracefully.
- Tests prove an old parser/compactor cannot erase v2 receipt state from a fenced mailbox.

**Verification:**
- Run migration/fence tests with simulated previous-version codec.
- Typecheck @wrongstack/core.

nodes.title: Storage-boundary enforcement of canonical send and actor authorization
nodes.description:
Make GlobalMailbox.send() and all mutation methods call validateSendType() / shared codec validation internally, and introduce actor-bearing service methods (sendFor, ackFor, softDeleteFor, restoreFor, registerFor, heartbeatFor). Legacy actor-ambiguous methods become explicitly internal/admin-only.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Direct typed calls to GlobalMailbox.send() reject invalid type/recipient combinations (control, broadcast assign/steer) without relying on transport adapters.
- Actor-bearing methods accept a trusted MailboxActorContext and reject unauthorized mutations.
- Legacy actor-ambiguous methods are marked @internal or deprecated in their JSDoc.
- Acknowledgement of a message not visible to the actor is rejected before persistence.
- No receipt or registry state is appended for rejected operations.
- Existing mailbox regression suites remain green after the change.

**Verification:**
- Run GlobalMailbox and storage-boundary tests.
- Typecheck @wrongstack/core.

nodes.title: Independent Global Mailbox P0 acceptance gate
nodes.description:
Perform independent contract, security, migration, and rollback review after all implementation and documentation tasks. Do not approve removal of legacy validation or compatibility controls without complete evidence.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- All twenty-four global acceptance criteria in the SDD have linked passing evidence.
- Cross-surface matrix passes with no undocumented exception.
- Migration/concurrency/security suite passes, including writer-version fence, old-compactor safety, previous-reader rollback compatibility, receipt fold algebra, and v1 completion classification.
- Core, CLI, WebUI server, and affected UI typechecks pass.
- Existing mailbox suites pass without skipped or zero-collected target files.
- Independent security review finds no Critical/High issue.
- Independent contract reviewer confirms actor-specific and aggregate fields are not conflated.
- Legacy code removal, if any, is limited to paths covered by parity fixtures.

**Verification:**
- Run all commands listed in SDD section 8.6 and the new P0 gate suite.
- Attach command outputs and reviewer verdicts before marking complete.
